title: Chesterton - The Sins Of Prince Saradine

evidence.paraphrase: Father Brown reacts with sudden alarm to the eerie moonlit landscape.
evidence.quote:
Father Brown sat bolt upright in the boat and crossed himself. His
      movement was so abrupt that his friend asked him, with a mild stare, what
      was the matter.

evidence.paraphrase: The priest contrasts the naive view of fairyland with the older, darker folklore understanding.
evidence.quote:
The people who wrote the mediaeval ballads," answered the priest, "knew
      more about fairies than you do. It isn	tu2019t only nice things that happen in
      fairyland.

evidence.paraphrase: The mirror-lined room multiplies the reflection of anyone entering, creating a disorienting effect.
evidence.quote:
It was a peculiarity of this glittering, glass-panelled place that
      anyone entering was reflected in four or five mirrors at once

evidence.paraphrase: Father Brown is disoriented by the many mirrored reflections, likening it to a dream.
evidence.quote:
Confound this crystal
      palace!" he muttered. "One sees everything too many times. It	tu2019s like a
      dream.

evidence.paraphrase: Father Brown reacts with horror and wishes to flee the house after the revelation.
evidence.quote:
Come away," said Father Brown, who was quite white. "Come away from this
      house of hell. Let us get into an honest boat again.

evidence.paraphrase: Father Brown begins explaining the scheme by which one man used his two enemies against each other.
evidence.quote:
A man had two enemies. He was a wise man. And so he discovered that
      two enemies are better than one.

evidence.paraphrase: Father Brown deduces a family connection by observing matching physical features.
evidence.quote:
The heavy brown eyes of Antonelli were the heavy brown
      eyes of Mrs. Anthony; and in a flash he saw half the story.
